scope: Static review of sequential suffix decoder and native ball-pass cleanup; no new test execution

original_findings.original: Native ball loop used finally-close, allowing decoder cleanup failure to replace a model or storage failure.
original_findings.resolution: Native ball branch catches BaseException, attempts decoder close, appends cleanup failure as a note, and re-raises the original. Successful iteration separately closes and surfaces cleanup failure. Decoder also retains primary decode errors and surfaces release failure when explicitly closed through GeneratorExit.

original_findings.original: Python bool was rejected but NumPy bool_ could enter through operator.index.
original_findings.resolution: The suffix start boundary now rejects both bool and np.bool_ before operator.index or decoder creation.

conclusions: Sequential decoding starts from the beginning and discards the prefix without yielding it to the inference consumer.
The independent decoder does not mutate the original random-access decoder position or frame cache.
The current native ball inference uses prefix zero and closes its decoder on success or failure.
No new concrete correctness or resource defect was found within the reviewed changes.
